import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_95/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_95/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_95/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_95/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_95/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_95/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_95/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source6_95_0 and Source6_95_2 on 'batsman'
# Rename columns to avoid collision and match intermediate_step1 schema
s0 = source0.rename(columns={"total_runs": "total_runs_x"})
s2 = source2.rename(columns={"total_runs": "total_runs_y"})
# Add batsman_runs_x and batsman_runs_y columns initialized to 0 for now (will fill later)
# But better to join with source1 and source3 to get batsman_runs_x and batsman_runs_y properly
# So first join s0 and s2 on batsman
step1 = pd.merge(s0, s2, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Step 2: Join Source6_95_1 and Source6_95_3 on 'batsman'
# Rename batsman_runs columns to batsman_runs_x and batsman_runs_y respectively
s1 = source1.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x"})
s3 = source3.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_y"})
step2 = pd.merge(s1, s3, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Step 3: Join Source6_95_4 and Source6_95_6 on 'batsman'
# Rename batsman_runs columns to batsman_runs_x_5 and batsman_runs_y_7 respectively
s4 = source4.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x_5"})
s6 = source6.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_y_7"})
step3 = pd.merge(s4, s6, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Step 4: Join Source6_95_0 and Source6_95_5 on 'batsman'
# source0 total_runs renamed to total_runs_x conflicts with source5 total_runs, so rename source5 total_runs to total_runs_y for clarity
s5 = source5.rename(columns={"total_runs": "total_runs_y"})
step4 = pd.merge(source0, s5, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Now we have:
# step1: batsman, total_runs_x, total_runs_y (from source0 and source2)
# step2: batsman, batsman_runs_x, batsman_runs_y (from source1 and source3)
# step3: batsman, batsman_runs_x_5, batsman_runs_y_7 (from source4 and source6)
# step4: batsman, total_runs (from source0), no of balls, batsman_runs, strike (from source5)

# We want to combine all these on batsman to get the final target schema:
# ['batsman': string,
#  'batsman_runs_x': float,
#  'total_runs_x': integer,
#  'total_runs_y': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_y': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_x_5': integer,
#  'no of balls': integer,
#  'batsman_runs_y_7': integer,
#  'strike': float,
#  'batsman_runs': integer]

# Merge step1 and step2 on batsman
df = pd.merge(step1, step2, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Merge with step3 on batsman
df = pd.merge(df, step3, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Merge with step4 on batsman
# step4 has total_runs (same as total_runs_x?), no of balls, batsman_runs, strike
# But step1 already has total_runs_x and total_runs_y from source0 and source2
# step4 total_runs is from source0, so rename to total_runs_x_2 to avoid confusion
step4_renamed = step4.rename(columns={"total_runs": "total_runs_x_2"})
df = pd.merge(df, step4_renamed, on="batsman", how="outer")

# Now fix columns:
# total_runs_x from step1 and total_runs_x_2 from step4 both come from source0 total_runs
# Prefer total_runs_x from step1, but if missing, fill from total_runs_x_2
df["total_runs_x"] = df["total_runs_x"].combine_first(df["total_runs_x_2"])

# Drop total_runs_x_2 column
df = df.drop(columns=["total_runs_x_2"])

# Fill missing numeric columns with 0 or appropriate types
# For batsman_runs_x, batsman_runs_y, batsman_runs_x_5, batsman_runs_y_7, no of balls, batsman_runs, strike, total_runs_x, total_runs_y
# Fill NaNs with 0 for numeric columns
numeric_cols = [
    "batsman_runs_x",
    "total_runs_x",
    "total_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_x_5",
    "no of balls",
    "batsman_runs_y_7",
    "strike",
    "batsman_runs",
]

for col in numeric_cols:
    if col in df.columns:
        # For strike, float fillna with 0.0
        if col == "strike":
            df[col] = df[col].fillna(0.0)
        else:
            df[col] = df[col].fillna(0)

# Convert columns to correct types as per target schema
df["batsman_runs_x"] = df["batsman_runs_x"].astype(float)
df["total_runs_x"] = df["total_runs_x"].astype(int)
df["total_runs_y"] = df["total_runs_y"].astype(int)
df["batsman_runs_y"] = df["batsman_runs_y"].astype(int)
df["batsman_runs_x_5"] = df["batsman_runs_x_5"].astype(int)
df["no of balls"] = df["no of balls"].astype(int)
df["batsman_runs_y_7"] = df["batsman_runs_y_7"].astype(int)
df["strike"] = df["strike"].astype(float)
df["batsman_runs"] = df["batsman_runs"].astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    "batsman",
    "batsman_runs_x",
    "total_runs_x",
    "total_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_x_5",
    "no of balls",
    "batsman_runs_y_7",
    "strike",
    "batsman_runs",
]

df = df[target_columns]

# Save to target path
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_95/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

    how="inner"
)

# Join Source6_95_1 and Source6_95_3 on 'batsman'
s1_3 = pd.merge(
    s1.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x"}),
    s3.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_y"}),

s4_6 = pd.merge(
    s4.rename(columns={"batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x_5"}),

    s1_3,

)

# Join s0_2_1_3 and s4_6 on 'batsman'
s_all = pd.merge(
    s0_2_1_3,
    s4_6,
    on="batsman",
    how="inner"
)

]
